why: Each order picks every item in a range, so item i is picked as often as the number of ranges covering it: a difference array plus a prefix sum. Then a query asks for the total pick count of items with value < q: sort items by value, prefix-sum their pick counts, and binary search.
hints: Item i contributes once per order whose range covers i. How do you count range coverage quickly?
Difference array over indices gives each item's pick count. A query then wants the sum of pick counts over items whose value is < q, which no longer depends on position.
Sort (value, count) pairs, build a prefix sum of counts, and for each query use bisect_left on the values. O((n + m + q) log n).
pitfalls: Strictly less than: use bisect_left, so items equal to the query are excluded.
Items picked by several orders count once per order.
Answers can exceed 32 bits (10^5 orders x 10^5 items).
